note: Examiner precedents. A repo file on purpose: every rule that can pre-fill a ruling must be readable, diffable and arguable in the planning chat, which a database row is not. ORDER MATTERS — most specific first. Matching stops at the first hit, so P1 must precede any general rule, or 'A is incorrect because...' reads as a plain reject. Nothing here writes a ruling; a precedent only ever produces a suggestion the founder confirms.

precedents.title: Wrong-option explanation
precedents.rationale: Pearson prints, under each MCQ, why each wrong option is wrong. It is feedback for the student who picked that option and it is not marking content: it awards nothing, rejects nothing, and must never reach the mark scheme. The option letter is read by distractor.ts, which refuses rather than guesses.

precedents.title: Transferred-error scope
precedents.rationale: TE and ecf lines say HOW to carry an error forward — which marks survive a wrong earlier answer. That qualifies the marking of points that already exist; it never adds one. Sits above P2 and the verb rules because 'Allow TE throughout' opens with Allow and would otherwise read as an Accept.

precedents.title: Significant-figure scope
precedents.rationale: An SF conditional is a permission and a condition in one sentence — 'Ignore SF except 1 SF' means do not penalise significant figures unless the answer is given to one. It scopes how an existing point is marked, so it is guidance, not a criterion and not an accept.

precedents.title: Tariff override
precedents.rationale: 'Correct answer with no working scores (4)' conditions a whole tariff: it says what a bare answer earns without changing what the points are. Recording it as a criterion would add a marking point and change what a student can score, which is precisely what it must not do.
